fix: Add Skillz MCP server even when no prior MCP config exists

Previously, handleMcpConfiguration would return early if rulerMcpJson was
null, preventing the Skillz MCP server from being added to agent configs
even when skills existed in .skillz directory.

This meant that projects relying on the new skills feature but without an
existing .ruler/mcp.json file would get skills copied to .skillz/ but
agent configuration would remain untouched, leaving skills unusable.

Changes:
- Remove rulerMcpJson null check from early return condition
- Allow filteredMcpJson to be null initially when rulerMcpJson is null
- Remove filteredMcpJson check from Skillz server addition condition
- Initialize empty MCP config when adding Skillz server to null config

Now agents that support MCP stdio but not native skills will get the
Skillz MCP server entry added even when starting from scratch.

Fixes P1 review comment about auto Skillz MCP server never being added
without existing mcp.json.

fix: Use atomic directory swap for skills propagation

Previously, propagateSkills() used naive recursive copySkillsDirectory()
calls which:
- Did not remove stale files deleted from source
- Left directories in inconsistent state if interrupted
- Could fail silently on partial copies

This was inconsistent with the atomic helpers propagateSkillsForClaude()
and propagateSkillsForSkillz() which properly implement temp-then-rename
strategy.

Changes:
- Replace copySkillsDirectory() calls with propagateSkillsForClaude()
- Replace copySkillsDirectory() calls with propagateSkillsForSkillz()
- Both helpers use atomic temp directory + rename approach
- Ensures stale files are removed and updates are all-or-nothing

The atomic strategy:
1. Copy skills to temporary directory (.tmp-{timestamp})
2. Remove existing target directory if present
3. Atomically rename temp directory to target
4. Clean up temp on any errors

This ensures skills directories stay consistent and match source exactly,
even if process is interrupted or fails mid-update.

Fixes P1 review comment about replacing skills copy with atomic swap.

fix: Clean up skills directories when skills are disabled

Previously, when skills were enabled and then later disabled (via
--no-skills CLI flag or [skills].enabled = false in ruler.toml), the
.claude/skills and .skillz directories would persist from the previous
run. This caused two problems:

1. Stale skills remained accessible even though skills were disabled
2. Skillz MCP server was still injected because it checked for .skillz
   directory existence rather than just respecting skillsEnabled flag

This violated the CLI > TOML > default precedence and made it impossible
to truly disable skills once they had been enabled.

Changes:
- Add cleanupSkillsDirectories() function to remove skills directories
- Call cleanup when propagateSkills() is invoked with skillsEnabled=false
- Remove .claude/skills and .skillz atomically
- Respect dry-run mode (log but don't delete)
- Add comprehensive tests for cleanup behavior

The cleanup ensures that:
- Stale skills don't persist when skills are disabled
- .skillz directory absence prevents Skillz MCP server injection
- Users can toggle skills on/off without manual cleanup

Fixes P1 review comments about respecting skills disable setting and
honoring skills.enabled configuration.

Test coverage:
- Tests removal of both .claude/skills and .skillz
- Tests dry-run mode (logs but doesn't remove)
- Tests graceful handling when directories don't exist

fix: Propagate skills for each nested .ruler directory

Previously, in nested mode, propagateSkills() was only called once with
the project root directory. This meant that skills placed alongside
nested .ruler directories (e.g. apps/foo/.ruler/skills) were silently
ignored and never copied to .claude/skills or .skillz for that nested
configuration.

This was inconsistent with how other configuration (rules, MCP settings)
is handled in nested mode, where each .ruler directory is processed
independently with its own configuration.

Changes:
- Loop through all hierarchicalConfigs in nested mode
- Call propagateSkills() for each nested directory's root
- Use path.dirname(configEntry.rulerDir) to get the correct root
- Add verbose logging for each nested skills propagation

This allows:
- Nested projects to have their own independent skills
- Skills to be placed next to nested .ruler directories
- Each nested config to opt in/out of skills independently
- Consistent behavior with other nested configuration features

Example:
Before: Only /project/.ruler/skills was processed
After:  Both /project/.ruler/skills AND /project/apps/foo/.ruler/skills
        are processed when in nested mode

Fixes P1 review comment about propagating skills for nested directories.

Test coverage:

- All 662 tests pass including nested configuration tests

fix: Add Skillz MCP server before calling agent.applyRulerConfig

Previously, Skillz MCP server worked for Copilot but not for Codex and
Gemini CLI. This was because:

1. Agents handle MCP configuration in two different ways:
   - External handling (Copilot, Cursor, etc): MCP config written by
     applyStandardMcpConfiguration in handleMcpConfiguration
   - Internal handling (Codex, Gemini, Zed, etc): MCP config written
     inside agent.applyRulerConfig()

2. The Skillz MCP server was only added in handleMcpConfiguration to
   filteredMcpJson, which only affects externally-handled agents

3. Agents with internal MCP handling received the original rulerMcpJson
   (without Skillz) in their applyRulerConfig() call at line 487

Root cause: The architecture has two code paths for MCP configuration,
and Skillz was only added to one path.

Solution:
- Add new addSkillzMcpServerIfNeeded() helper function
- Call it BEFORE agent.applyRulerConfig() to augment rulerMcpJson
- Pass augmented version to all agents in applyConfigurationsToAgents
- This ensures both internal and external MCP handling get Skillz

The fix ensures Skillz server is available to ALL agents that:
- Support MCP stdio (supportsMcpStdio() returns true)
- Don't have native skills support (supportsNativeSkills() returns false)
- Have skills enabled (skillsEnabled = true)
- Have .skillz directory with propagated skills

Implementation details:
- addSkillzMcpServerIfNeeded checks if any agent needs Skillz
- Only adds Skillz if .skillz directory exists
- Returns augmented config or original if no changes needed
- Works in both dry-run and normal modes

Test coverage:
- 6 comprehensive integration tests covering:
  - Codex CLI config (.codex/config.toml)
  - Gemini CLI config (.gemini/settings.json)
  - Copilot config (.vscode/mcp.json)
  - Skills disabled behavior
  - Existing MCP servers coexistence
  - Multiple agents simultaneously

All 668 tests pass, including new integration tests.

Fix GitHub CLI authentication in workflow

Use echo to pipe token instead of here-string syntax which doesn't work properly with secret interpolation in GitHub Actions.

Remove redundant GitHub CLI authentication step

GitHub CLI automatically uses GH_TOKEN environment variable for authentication, so the explicit gh auth login step is not needed and actually causes an error.

Authenticate gh CLI before running Copilot CLI

Copilot CLI requires gh to be authenticated. This adds an explicit authentication step that doesn't set environment variables during auth to avoid conflicts.

Set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable for Copilot CLI

While gh auth login succeeds, Copilot CLI needs GITHUB_TOKEN set as an environment variable to find the authentication.

Use fine-grained COPILOT_CLI_TOKEN for authentication

Switch from COPILOT_PAT to COPILOT_CLI_TOKEN which is a fine-grained
Personal Access Token with the 'copilot requests' scope required for
programmatic authentication in GitHub Actions.

Based on research from GitHub issue #233, the new Copilot CLI requires
fine-grained tokens with the copilot requests scope, not classic PATs.

Remove obsolete Codex CLI config.toml

This configuration file was used by the old Codex CLI and is no longer
needed now that we're using GitHub Copilot CLI instead.

Remove redundant gh auth login step

Copilot CLI can authenticate directly via GITHUB_TOKEN environment
variable with a fine-grained token. The gh auth login step is not
necessary and may even interfere.

Use --model flag instead of COPILOT_MODEL environment variable

Specify GPT-5 model using the --model gpt-5 command-line flag as per
Copilot CLI documentation.

Add native skills support for Roo Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Amp, and Kilo Code

This PR adds native skills support for 5 new agents that have implemented the
SKILL.md format:

## Changes by Agent

### Roo Code
- Skills directory: `.roo/skills/`
- Added `supportsNativeSkills()` method to RooCodeAgent
- Added `propagateSkillsForRoo()` function in SkillsProcessor
- Documentation: https://docs.roocode.com/features/skills

### Gemini CLI
- Skills directory: `.gemini/skills/`
- Added `supportsNativeSkills()` method to GeminiCliAgent
- Added `propagateSkillsForGemini()` function in SkillsProcessor
- Documentation: https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/

### Cursor
- Skills directory: `.cursor/skills/`
- Added `supportsNativeSkills()` method to CursorAgent
- Added `propagateSkillsForCursor()` function in SkillsProcessor
- Documentation: https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills

### Amp
- Skills directory: `.agents/skills/` (shared with Goose)
- Added `supportsNativeSkills()` method to AmpAgent
- Uses existing `propagateSkillsForGoose()` function
- Documentation: https://ampcode.com/news/agent-skills

### Kilo Code
- Skills directory: `.claude/skills/` (shared with Claude Code)
- Added `supportsNativeSkills()` method to KiloCodeAgent
- Uses existing `propagateSkillsForClaude()` function

feat(subagents): add capability flag for native subagent support

Add optional supportsNativeSubagents() method to IAgent, mirroring the
existing supportsNativeSkills() pattern. Implement on Claude Code, Cursor,
OpenAI Codex CLI, and GitHub Copilot — the four agents that have shipped
a native subagent primitive.

feat(subagents): add discovery, per-agent transformers, and orchestrator

Introduce .ruler/agents/<name>.md as the source format, with YAML
frontmatter (name, description, tools, model, readonly, is_background).

SubagentsUtils parses and validates frontmatter using js-yaml (already a
project dependency) and provides a Claude-to-Copilot tool alias map.

SubagentsProcessor discovers source files, dispatches per-agent
propagators, and writes target files atomically (stage to temp dir,
rename into place — same pattern as SkillsProcessor):

  - Claude  → .claude/agents/<name>.md         (frontmatter passthrough)
  - Cursor  → .cursor/agents/<name>.md         (drops tools, applies
                                                Cursor defaults)
  - Codex   → .codex/agents/<name>.toml        (one self-contained TOML
                                                file per agent, with
                                                inline developer_instructions)
  - Copilot → .github/agents/<name>.md         (tools mapped from Claude
                                                vocabulary to Copilot
                                                aliases; readonly maps
                                                to disable-model-invocation)

The orchestrator handles cleanup-on-disable: when subagents are turned
off, all four target directories are removed on the next apply.

feat(subagents): wire CLI flag and ruler.toml configuration

Add --subagents / --no-subagents flags to ruler apply, and a [subagents]
section to ruler.toml. Precedence matches skills: CLI flag > TOML setting
> default (enabled).

Existing handler tests are updated for the new positional argument on
applyAllAgentConfigs.

feat(subagents): integrate with apply pipeline and gitignore

Call propagateSubagents() inside applyAllAgentConfigs for both single and
nested-config code paths. Add subagent target directories
(.claude/agents/, .cursor/agents/, .codex/agents/, .github/agents/) to
the Ruler-managed gitignore block when subagents are enabled.

docs(subagents): add Subagents Support section and supported-agents column

Add a new "Subagents Support (Experimental)" section after the existing
skills section, mirroring its structure: how it works, source format,
configuration, validation, dry-run mode, .gitignore integration,
limitations, and an example workflow.

Add a "Subagents Support / Location" column to the Supported AI Agents
table and document --subagents / --no-subagents in the apply Options
table.

fix(subagents): preserve readonly and is_background in Claude propagation

The Claude propagator dropped readonly and is_background from source
frontmatter, even when the user authored them explicitly. Claude Code
ignores unknown frontmatter keys but downstream tools that read
.claude/agents/*.md can use them. Pass them through verbatim so authoring
intent survives the transform.

Update the Claude propagation test to assert the values are preserved.

fix(subagents): handle malformed YAML frontmatter as validation warning

js-yaml throws on invalid YAML, which previously aborted the entire
discovery pass instead of degrading to a per-file warning. One bad
.ruler/agents/*.md file would prevent every other valid subagent from
being propagated.

Wrap parseFrontmatter in a try/catch inside loadSubagentFile and surface
the parse error using the same {valid: false, error} shape as the other
validation failures. discoverSubagents continues iterating, and the bad
file is reported alongside any others via the existing warnings channel.

fix(subagents): reconcile stale target directories when state shrinks

The previous orchestrator wrote the current set of targets but never
removed managed directories that fell out of scope. Two scenarios were
broken:

1. User narrows --agents (e.g. claude+cursor → claude only): the stale
   .cursor/agents/ directory remained as orphaned, out-of-sync config.

2. User deletes or empties .ruler/agents/ but leaves [subagents]
   enabled = true: the previously generated target directories were
   left untouched, so the agents kept reading stale subagents.

Reconcile both cases:
- When the source directory is missing or yields no valid subagents,
  run the existing cleanupAllSubagentsDirectories helper.
- After computing the active targets set, remove any managed target
  directory whose target is not in the set. The selected target dirs
  are then (re)written by the per-agent propagators below.

fix(subagents): gate Copilot tool-drop warnings behind --verbose / --dry-run

The Copilot transformer dropped any source tools that lack a Copilot
alias mapping, but it always logged a warning to stderr. That meant
every normal apply (no verbose, no dry-run) would emit a warning for
each subagent with a Claude-only tool, which is noisy and inconsistent
with what the README and PR description promised.

Tool-drop is informational, not an error. Gate the warning so:

- A normal apply stays silent (the dropped tools simply don't appear in
  the generated .github/agents/<name>.md frontmatter).
- --verbose surfaces every dropped tool so users can audit the mapping.
- --dry-run also surfaces them, since the point of dry-run is to preview
  what an apply would change.

Thread `verbose` into PropagateOptions and pass it through the orchestrator
to all four per-agent propagators. Update the README copy to match the
new contract.

Tests added in subagents-propagation.test.ts spy on console.warn to
verify all three modes (silent / verbose / dry-run).

feat(agents): exclude .ruler/agents from rules; rename [subagents] → [agents]

Stops subagent definitions from leaking into top-level rule files and
aligns the TOML config key with the directory name.

- `.ruler/agents/*.md` are no longer concatenated into generated rule
  files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, Copilot instructions, etc.). Same
  skip-behavior as `.ruler/skills/`.
- New `[agents] include_in_rules = true` opts back in for users who
  want the markdown bodies appended to the top-level rules.
- `[agents] enabled = …` replaces `[subagents] enabled = …` for native
  subagent propagation. Legacy `[subagents]` is still honored with a
  one-time deprecation warning per process; new keys take precedence
  per-key when both are present.
- Default `agents.enabled` flips to `false`. Subagent runtime prompts
  are now opt-in.
- `[agents]` is a heterogeneous TOML table — reserved booleans
  (`enabled`, `include_in_rules`) live alongside per-coding-agent
  records (`[agents.claude]`, …). Unknown scalar keys under `[agents]`
  fail Zod validation with an actionable error.
- Independence: `[agents].enabled` (subagent propagation) and
  `[agents.<name>].enabled` (per-coding-agent output) flow through
  separate code paths and never imply each other.

Implementation notes

- `readMarkdownFiles(rulerDir, { includeAgents })` gets an explicit
  option; both `apply-engine` call sites load config first and pass
  the derived flag.
- `cloneLoadedConfig` now preserves `skills` and `subagents` (latent
  bug in nested mode that silently dropped these sections).
- Tracks skipped agent subtrees so a stale generated root AGENTS.md
  isn't resurrected when `.ruler/agents` was the only source under
  `.ruler`.

Tests

- New behavior matrix: `tests/subagents-rules-concatenation.test.ts`
  covers all 5 rows (propagate × include_in_rules) plus legacy
  `[subagents]` fallback + per-key precedence + deprecation warning.
- New unit tests for `readMarkdownFiles` agents-skip option,
  `SubagentsUtils` validate/parse/map, `SubagentsProcessor` dry-run +
  cleanup + reconcile + Copilot model handling, and `RuleProcessor`
  baseDir fallback.
- ConfigLoader tests for `[agents]` reserved keys, legacy fallback,
  once-per-process warning, Zod validation, and independence in both
  directions.
- 908 tests pass.
